statement: If the side of the hexagon and that of the decagon inscribed in the same circle be added together, the whole straight line has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and its greater segment is the side of the hexagon.
heath_proof: Let ABC be a circle; of the figures inscribed in the circle ABC let BC be the side of a decagon, CD that of a hexagon, and let them be in a straight line; I say that the whole straight line BD has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and CD is its greater segment. For let the centre of the circle, the point E, be taken, let EB, EC, ED be joined, and let BE be carried through to A. Since BC is the side of an equilateral decagon, therefore the circumference ACB is five times the circumference BC; therefore the circumference AC is quadruple of CB. But, as the circumference AC is to CB, so is the angle AEC to the angle CEB; [VI. 33] therefore the angle AEC is quadruple of the angle CEB. And, since the angle EBC is equal to the angle ECB, [I. 5] therefore the angle AEC is double of the angle ECB. [I. 32] And, since the straight line EC is equal to CD, for each of them is equal to the side of the hexagon inscribed in the circle ABC, [IV. 15] the angle CED is also equal to the angle CDE; [I. 5] therefore the angle ECB is double of the angle EDC. [I. 32] But the angle AEC was proved double of the angle ECB; therefore the angle AEC is quadruple of the angle EDC. But the angle AEC was also proved quadruple of the angle BEC; therefore the angle EDC is equal to the angle BEC. But the angle EBD is common to the two triangles BEC and BED; therefore the remaining angle BED is also equal to the remaining angle ECB; [I. 32] therefore the triangle EBD is equiangular with the triangle EBC. Therefore, proportionally, as DB is to BE, so is EB to BC. [VI. 4] But EB is equal to CD. Therefore, as BD is to DC, so is DC to CB. And BD is greater than DC; therefore DC is also greater than CB. Therefore the straight line BD has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and DC is its greater segment.
ai_proof_text:
13.9
**Statement:** If the side of the hexagon and that of the decagon inscribed in the same circle be added together, the whole straight line has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and its greater segment is the side of the hexagon.

**Step 1.** Let ABC be a circle; let BC be the side of the equilateral decagon inscribed in it and CD the side of the hexagon inscribed in the same circle, and let BC and CD be placed in a straight line, so that BCD is one straight line. I say that BD is cut in extreme and mean ratio at C, and that CD is its greater segment.

**Step 2.** Take the centre E of the circle [3.1]; join EB, EC, ED [P1]; and produce BE beyond E to meet the circumference again at A [P2]. Since E is the centre, EA = EB = EC [D1.15].

**Step 3.** BA passes through the centre and is terminated at both ends by the circumference; it is therefore a diameter and bisects the circle [D1.17], so the circumference ACB is half of the whole circumference. Since the ten equal sides of the inscribed decagon cut off ten equal circumferences [3.28], the whole circumference is ten times the circumference BC; hence the circumference ACB is five times the circumference BC. Taking away the circumference BC from the circumference ACB, the remaining circumference AC is four times the circumference CB [CN3].

**Step 4.** The angles AEC and CEB at the centre stand on the circumferences AC and CB respectively, and angles in the same circle have the same ratio as the circumferences on which they stand [6.33]; therefore, since circumference AC is four times circumference CB, angle AEC is four times angle CEB.

**Step 5.** In triangle EBC, EB = EC, so angle ECB = angle EBC [1.5]. Since BE is produced to A, angle AEC is the exterior angle of triangle EBC at E, and equals the sum of the two interior and opposite angles EBC and ECB [1.32]; therefore angle AEC is double angle ECB.

**Step 6.** CD is the side of the hexagon inscribed in the circle, and the side of the inscribed hexagon equals the radius of the circle [4.15]; so CD = EC [CN1]. Hence in triangle ECD, angle CED = angle CDE [1.5]. Since DC is produced to B (BCD being a straight line), angle ECB is the exterior angle of triangle ECD at C, and equals the sum of the interior and opposite angles CED and CDE [1.32]; therefore angle ECB is double angle EDC.

**Step 7.** Angle AEC is double angle ECB (Step 5) and angle ECB is double angle EDC (Step 6); therefore angle AEC is four times angle EDC. But angle AEC is also four times angle CEB (Step 4). Hence four times angle CEB equals four times angle EDC [CN1], and so angle EDC = angle CEB.

**Step 8.** Consider triangles EBD and EBC. The angle at B is common to both (angle EBD is the same angle as angle EBC, since C lies on BD), and angle EDB = angle BEC (Step 7). Since the three angles of every triangle are together equal to two right angles [1.32], the remaining angle BED of triangle EBD equals the remaining angle ECB of triangle EBC. Therefore triangle EBD is equiangular with triangle EBC.

**Step 9.** In equiangular triangles the sides about the equal angles are proportional, those which subtend the equal angles being corresponding [6.4]. The side DB subtends angle BED and the side EB subtends the equal angle ECB; the side BE subtends angle EDB and the side BC subtends the equal angle BEC. Therefore DB : BE = EB : BC.

**Step 10.** Now BE = CD, both being equal to the radius EC (Steps 2 and 6). Equal magnitudes have the same ratio to the same magnitude, and the same magnitude has the same ratio to equal magnitudes [5.7]; so DB : BE = DB : CD and EB : BC = CD : BC. Ratios which are the same with the same ratio are also the same with one another [5.11]; therefore BD : DC = DC : CB.

**Step 11.** BD is greater than its part DC [CN5]. In the proportion BD : DC = DC : CB the first term BD exceeds the third term DC; therefore the second term DC exceeds the fourth term CB [5.14]. Thus DC is the greater and CB the lesser segment of BD.

**Step 12.** As the whole BD is to its greater segment DC, so is the greater segment DC to the lesser segment CB; therefore BD has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at C [D6.3], and its greater segment DC is the side of the hexagon. Q.E.D.
